classification.difficultyReason: Translate neighbouring averages into two simultaneous equations and solve by elimination.

content.prompt: Find the values of $x$ and $y$ in the figure below if each unknown number is equal to the average of its neighbours.

spec.description: Four equal unfilled circles connected horizontally in the order 3, x, y, 8. Decorative cyan outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: The neighbours of x are 3 and y; the neighbours of y are x and 8.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied labels 3, x, y and 8 appear.

answer.short:
$(x,y)=\left(\frac{14}{3},\frac{19}{3}\right)$.

Write an equation for each average, then eliminate $y$.
answer.worked:
Each unknown equals the average of its two neighbours:
$$\begin{align*}
x&=\frac{3+y}{2}\\
y&=\frac{x+8}{2}.
\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}
2x-y&=3\qquad(1)\\
-x+2y&=8\qquad(2).
\end{align*}$$
Adding twice (1) to (2):
$$\begin{align*}
3x&=14\\
x&=\frac{14}{3}.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (1):
$$\begin{align*}
y&=2\left(\frac{14}{3}\right)-3\\
y&=\frac{19}{3}.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $(x,y)=\left(\frac{14}{3},\frac{19}{3}\right)$.
